title: Resilience Libraries: Polly & Hystrix
description: Implement resilience using Polly (.NET) and Resilience4j (Java).

data.text: Resilience libraries provide built-in implementations of resilience patterns. Polly (.NET) and Resilience4j (Java) are popular choices.

terms.definition: A resilience library for Java, successor to Hystrix.
Netflix resilience library (deprecated in favor of Resilience4j).
A reusable resilience strategy in Polly.

items: Retry, circuit breaker, timeout, bulkhead, fallback
Circuit breaker, rate limiter, retry, bulkhead, time limiter

data.text: Polly allows composing policies. For example, wrap a retry policy around a circuit breaker around a timeout policy.

data.caption: Polly Policy Composition
data.definition:
flowchart TD
    Client[Client] --> Timeout[Timeout Policy]
    Timeout --> CB[Circuit Breaker Policy]
    CB --> Retry[Retry Policy]
    Retry --> Fallback[Fallback Policy]
    Fallback --> Service[Service Call]

data.title: Polly Policy Composition
data.code:
var policy = Policy
    .Handle<Exception>()
    .FallbackAsync(async (ct) => new HttpResponseMessage(HttpStatusCode.ServiceUnavailable))
    .WrapAsync(Policy
        .Handle<HttpRequestException>()
        .CircuitBreakerAsync(5, TimeSpan.FromSeconds(30)))
    .WrapAsync(Policy
        .Handle<HttpRequestException>()
        .WaitAndRetryAsync(3, attempt => TimeSpan.FromSeconds(Math.Pow(2, attempt))))
    .WrapAsync(Policy.TimeoutAsync<HttpResponseMessage>(TimeSpan.FromSeconds(10)));

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Polly and Resilience4j provide built-in patterns
Order matters: fallback outermost, innermost call
data.takeaway: Use resilience libraries to implement patterns correctly.
